title: [Feature] Route strided MLA cache writes through PROLOG_V3
body:
### What does this PR do?

Replaces the `npu_kv_rmsnorm_rope_cache` writer with `npu_mla_prolog_v3` for strided MLA caches on A2/A3/A5.

### Key changes

- Route component-major and token-fused MLA caches through `npu_mla_prolog_v3`
- Reuse the PROLOG_V3 weight preparation path for DSpark context writes
- Add CPU routing tests for:
  - A2/A3 component-major cache
  - A5 token-fused cache
  - decode/prefill routing
  - FA-quant query mode

### Why is this needed?

`aclnnKvRmsNormRopeCache` marks cache inputs as `AutoContiguous`, which can materialize a large contiguous copy for strided MLA caches and cause OOM during graph warmup. `npu_mla_prolog_v3` marks the cache inputs as `IgnoreContiguous` and supports the strided cache layout directly.

### Notes

- This PR is based on the strided MLA cache work from #16456.
- The baseline PR keeps the existing `rmsnorm_rope` path; this PR switches the writer to PROLOG_V3.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/8cc9aa5ad350f6f80cf3bebb298d410803ff75a9
